The first recorded travels by Europeans to China and back date from this time. The most famous traveler of the period was the Venetian Marco Polo, whose account of his trip to "Cambaluc," the capital of the Great Khan, and of life there astounded the people of Europe. The account of his travels, Il milione (or, The Million, known in English as the Travels of Marco Polo), appeared about the year 1299. Some argue over the accuracy of Marco Polo's accounts due to the lack of mentioning the Great Wall of China, tea houses, which would have been a prominent sight since Europeans had yet to adopt a tea culture, as well the practice of foot binding by the women in capital of the Great Khan. Some suggest that Marco Polo acquired much of his knowledge through contact with Persian traders since many of the places he named were in Persian. ## One-hot representation

Different words should have different vectors

Assign each word a unique sparse vector.

Vocabulary table: [cat, dog, car, apple, run]

cat => [1,0,0,0,0]

dog => [0, 1, 0, 0, 0]

car => [0, 0, 1, 0, 0]

apple => [0, 0, 0, 1, 0]

run => [0, 0, 0, 0, 1]

Q: What are the issues with representing a word this way?

A: All words are equally (dis)similar; e.g., the dot products for (cat, dog) and (cat, car) are both zero

## Limitations of recurrent language models

Learning bottleneck: Information decay

Information from $x_{i}$ must pass through many updates to affect $h_{t}$.

System inefficiency

■ Sequential computation: $h_{t}$ depends on $h_{t-1}$.

Training/serving large models becomes cost-prohibitive due to time constraints.

Each server is equipped with eight GPUs and two CPUs. Within a server, the eight GPUs are connected via NVLink. Training jobs are scheduled using MAST (Choudhury et al., 2024), Meta’s global-scale training scheduler.
